Brookfield Asset Management Has Lowered Southwestern Energy Co (SWN) Stake as Share Price Declined; As Apple (AAPL) Stock Value Declined, Alethea Capital Management Has Upped Holding
May 26, 2018 - By Vivian Currie
Brookfield Asset Management Inc decreased its stake in Southwestern Energy Co (SWN) by 20% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Brookfield Asset Management Inc sold 100,000 shares as the company’s stock declined 19.55% with the market. The hedge fund held 400,000 shares of the oil & gas production company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $2.23 million, down from 500,000 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Brookfield Asset Management Inc who had been investing in Southwestern Energy Co for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $2.59 billion market cap company. It closed at $4.45 lastly. It is down 44.42% since May 26, 2017 and is downtrending. It has underperformed by 55.97% the S&P500.
Alethea Capital Management Llc increased its stake in Apple Inc (AAPL) by 188.4% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Alethea Capital Management Llc bought 1,884 shares as the company’s stock declined 3.81% with the market. The institutional investor held 2,884 shares of the computer manufacturing company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $488,000, up from 1,000 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Alethea Capital Management Llc who had been investing in Apple Inc for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $926.90B market cap company. The stock increased 0.23% or $0.43 during the last trading session, reaching $188.58. About 15.45 million shares traded. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has risen 19.49% since May 26, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 7.94% the S&P500.
Analysts await Southwestern Energy Company (NYSE:SWN) to report earnings on August, 2. They expect $0.16 EPS, up 100.00% or $0.08 from last year’s $0.08 per share. SWN’s profit will be $93.09M for 6.95 P/E if the $0.16 EPS becomes a reality. After $0.28 actual EPS reported by Southwestern Energy Company for the previous quarter, Wall Street now forecasts -42.86% negative EPS growth.
